artworks.title: Vox Dei, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image shows a central figure with flowing hair and a beard, appearing ethereal and serene. The figure is standing or hovering in a divine position, with eyes gazing downward. The being is dressed in a robe and holds a triangular frame filled with illustrations and text. Various scenes within the frame depict figures in historical European attire. Surrounding the figure are intricate engravings, including clouds, allegorical figures, lion-like creatures, and a skeletal figure with text about death. The background features etched textures, enhancing a celestial theme.

artworks.title: Vox Dei, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image shows a full-body depiction of a bearded man with long hair. He is positioned centrally in the composition with his eyes closed and a calm expression. He is wearing a flowing robe and his arms are extended downwards, holding a triangular structure. Inside the triangle are several smaller portraits of individuals. Two full-length figures, seemingly younger men, are depicted at the bottom corners of the triangle, both wearing elaborate historical clothing. Below the triangle is a scene with skeletal figures and grim imagery. The background features celestial elements, swirling clouds above, architectural details on the sides, and inscriptions. Symbolic imagery such as a lion and another mythical creature can be seen at the far sides of the composition.

artworks.title: Vox Regis, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a royal figure on a throne surrounded by courtiers and soldiers. The central figure is on a throne, dressed in robes and holding a sceptre and orb. Flanking the throne are soldiers holding swords and courtiers with bowed heads. The room has arched windows, symmetry, and balance in the composition. The embedded text refers to wisdom, authority, and obedience. The drawing shows attention to detail in the clothing and expressions of the figures. It captures a moment of ceremonial significance, possibly a scene of homage or coronation.

artworks.title: Title Page for Vox Populi Eoricum, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image shows a man holding a walking cane, wearing a wide-brimmed hat, fur-lined cloak, decorative top, knee-length pants, lace ruff, and a sword. He has a pendant hanging from a chain around his neck. Beside him is a wooden chair with a circular cutout on the seat and in the background, there is a horse-drawn carriage. Text appears at the top and bottom of the image.

artworks.title: Title Page for Vox Populi Eoricum, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image depicts a man standing upright, slightly to the side, facing forward with a composed expression. He has a beard and wears a wide-brimmed hat, fur-lined cloak, patterned doublet, breeches, large ruff, and a medallion on a chain. He holds a long staff. In the background, there is a horse-drawn carriage, a building, and a wood chair with an open circular seat, all connected to ornate text resembling a page.

artworks.title: The Spanish Parliament from Vox Populi Eoricum, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image depicts a group of figures in period attire seated around a large table in a formal setting. Two crowns and a scepter are placed on the table. The room has lattice-patterned windows and a door with a coat of arms. The figures are detailed in elaborate clothing and headwear, indicating a scene of political or royal discussions.

artworks.title: True Portraiture of the Jesuits and Priests from Vox Populi, by Thomas Scott
artworks.artist: Attributed to Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: There is a drawing of a group of Jesuits and priests seated around a table. The scene is detailed, showing a formal gathering of religious figures, each identified by their names above them. The figures are dressed in clergy attire, with religious items on the table. The room has two diamond-paned windows. The caption at the top reads, "I have here sett the true portrature of the Iesuits and priests," and the one at the bottom concludes with, "as they vse to sitt at Counsell in England to further the Catholicke Cause." The line work and shading create depth and texture.

artworks.title: Title Page to De Origine Moribus by Joanne Leslaeo
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing the title page of an old book. The page includes Latin text on aged paper, with the title "De Origine Moribus & rebus gestis Scotorum" translating to "On the Origin, Manners & Deeds of the Scots." The author, "Joanne Leslæo," is identified as the bishop of Ross. An illustration resembling a heraldic crest or emblem with intricate details is also present. The publication information indicates that the book was printed in Rome in 1578 and reissued in 1675.

artworks.title: Fergus I of Scotland With Geneology
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a genealogical chart. The image displays a detailed historical family tree of Scottish kings. In the center is an image labeled as "FERGUSIUS" (Fergus), depicted in an ornate circle, holding a scepter and wearing a crown. Surrounding the central figure are interconnected circles containing names, each topped with a crown graphic. At the top right, an intricate coat of arms is depicted. Latin text is present throughout, providing detailed explanations of the lineage and illustrating the connections of Scottish royalty through generations. The style is reminiscent of genealogical charts from medieval and Renaissance periods, emphasizing the importance of heritage and succession.

artworks.title: Donald I of Scotland with Geneology
artworks.description: The image shows a genealogical chart with royal heraldry and regalia. It features a central crowned figure in a circular medallion, surrounded by smaller circles connected by lines outlining a family lineage. The central figure has a crown and scepter and is accompanied by heraldic symbols, including a crest with a lion rampant. Various Latin names enclosed in circles are linked to show familial connections and hierarchy. The title reads "STEMMA II REGVM XIII."

artworks.title: Fergus II of Scotland with Geneology
artworks.description: The image displays a historical genealogy chart with a portrait of a man shown in profile. He has a beard, curly hair, and wears a crown and robe. The central portrait is surrounded by interconnected circles containing names and symbols, with each circle topped by a crown. To the right is an ornate coat of arms with a crown and two crossed scepters. The background is a parchment, and there is Latin text present.

artworks.title: Achaius of Scotland, with Geneology
artworks.description: This is a genealogical chart depicting a royal lineage, presumably of Scottish origin. The chart displays a detailed family tree with names in circles connected by lines. At the top center, there is a circular portrait labeled as "Achaius Scotorum Rex," surrounded by heraldic symbols. Another crest is shown on the right supported by a lion and unicorn. The names on the chart are topped with small crowns and accompanied by Latin text. The overall presentation is typical of genealogical manuscripts from that period.

artworks.title: Malcolm III with Geneology
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a genealogy chart featuring royal lineage. The drawing displays a family tree, focusing particularly on the lineage of Malcolm III of Scotland. At the top of the chart, there is a detailed depiction of a crowned figure, labeled as "MALCOLMVS Canmoir III Scotor Rex," surrounded by text in a Latin script. Various branches extend from the central portrait, linking to other circles that contain names and titles, some adorned with crowns indicating their royal status. An elaborate coat of arms is also illustrated to the right of the portrait.

artworks.title: Robert de Bruce VIII, King of Scotland
artworks.description: This is a detailed genealogical chart featuring Robert the Bruce, King of Scots. The chart includes an ornate circular portrait of Robert in the center, surrounded by his title "ROBERTVS BRVSEVS SCOT. REX." A family crest or coat of arms is depicted to the right of the portrait. The chart consists of interconnected circles with names and titles indicating family members and relationships. Latin inscriptions are present, providing historical context and lineage notations. The chart is carefully designed with lines and connections to illustrate familial ties, marriages, and descendants of Robert the Bruce.

artworks.title: James II of Scotland with Geneology of the Stuarts
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving featuring the profile of a man's bust surrounded by a circular frame labeled "IACOBVS SEVNDVS SCOTORVM REX," symbolizing a king named James II of Scotland. The man is depicted from the shoulders up, in a left-facing profile, wearing a crown adorned with small crosses and a fur-trimmed cape or robe. His facial features include a prominent nose, a short beard, and tightly curled hair. The frame has a Latin inscription and above it, a coat of arms with a lion and unicorn is partially visible. In the background, there is a complex genealogical chart with circles connected by lines, each labeled with Latin names and titles. The paper has a textured appearance, suggesting it may be a historical document.

artworks.title: James V of Scotland with Geneology
artworks.description: The image features an engraving of a man shown from the chest up, in a circular medallion at the center. The man is in profile, facing right, wearing a crown adorned with pearls and intricate patterns. His features are robust, with a prominent nose and curly hair under the crown. He is dressed in regal clothing with layers and embellishments. The text reads "IACOBUS V SCOTORUM REX CVD," identifying him as King James V of Scotland. Below the portrait is a family tree diagram linking him to others, including his daughter and grandson. On the right is a heraldic coat of arms with two unicorns holding a shield and royal symbols above. The background has Latin text about the subject. The paper is yellowed with visible texture and a slightly torn edge.

artworks.title: Family Tree of the Stuarts Stemming From Banquho
artworks.description: This is a print depicting a family tree. It is filled with text that seems to identify various people and their relationships. The central tree winds through the middle of the print like a snake, and branches on either side are adorned with rose-like floral decorations and circular medallions containing names. Some of the circles towards the top of the tree have crowns on them. Ornate coats of arms are included next to the tree, with the largest one near the top left corner. There are several lines of text at the top of the print. The background is beige paper.

artworks.title: Mary Queen of Scots with James VI of Scotlandand I of England
artworks.description: The image features two portrait-style engravings set within an elaborate design. The upper portrait shows a woman wearing a crown with long hair styled around her shoulders. The lower portrait features a young boy with curly hair and wearing a high-collared garment. The illustrations are surrounded by Latin inscriptions, decorative scrolls, and a heraldic emblem at the bottom. The entire illustration is framed within a rectangular piece of paper with an aged appearance.

artworks.title: Coat of Arms -- Mary, Queen of Scots
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a coat of arms with text beneath it. The image features a heraldic shield with a lion rampant, flanked by two lions. Above the shield are a crown and decorative elements, including flags. Below the drawing, there is a block of text in Latin, beginning with the title 'Ad Sereni[ssimam] Scotorum Reginam, MARIAM,' followed by more text. The piece is presented on aged, yellowed paper with slightly rough edges.

artworks.title: Stuart Coat of Arms from Vera Descriptio by John Jonston
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a heraldic coat of arms. The image features a shield with a rampant lion at its center. The shield is supported by a mythical unicorn on the left and a horse-like creature on the right, each standing on their hind legs and holding spears. Above the shield is a helmet adorned with feathers and crowned with a lion holding a dagger and a scepter. The design includes floral and decorative elements and banners displaying the words "IN DEFENCE." The drawing showcases elaborate engravings typical of heraldic illustrations.

artworks.title: Later Copy of the Arms of Scotland
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a heraldic coat of arms. It features two unicorns and a crowned lion crest. The artwork shows a symmetrical composition, with two crowned unicorns on either side of a central shield. The shield displays a lion rampant. Above the shield, a crowned lion holds a sword and a scepter atop a helmet surrounded by mantling. Below the shield is a banner with the Latin motto "Nemo Me Impune Lacesset." The design includes flourishes, scrollwork, and two flags flanking the unicorns, one with a lion and the other with a saltire.

artworks.title: Robert II, King of Scotland
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of a man's upper body. He is facing slightly to the left, with his gaze directed towards the viewer's left. The man has detailed facial features, including heavy eyelids, high cheekbones, and a subtle expression. He has long wavy hair under a crown with a jewel and fur trim. The man wears regal clothing with a fur-collared mantle and a patterned garment. He holds a book or document in his left hand. The background has decorative elements like stylized leaves, and the image is framed with ornate borders. Latin text below the image identifies him as Robertus II, King of Scots, with additional Latin inscription underneath.

artworks.title: Robert III, King of Scotland
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man depicted from the waist up. He is seated upright in a formal pose, looking slightly to his left. His facial features are well-defined with prominent eyes and straight lips. He has medium-length hair which flows from beneath a decorative hat adorned with a pattern and a prominent jewel at the front. The man's clothing is regal, featuring a high collar and an embroidered robe with elaborate detailing on the shoulders. He holds an object that appears to be a ring with a small jewel in his right hand. The background of the portrait is intricately designed with symmetrical patterns and a decorative border surrounding the oval frame of the image. The lower part of the image includes text inscription in Latin.

artworks.title: James I, King of Scotland
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait depicting the upper body of a man who is positioned facing slightly to the right, with his head turned to the side. He has long, flowing hair and a distinct beard and mustache that are parted in the middle. The man is wearing a crown adorned with circular decorative elements. He is clothed in a regal-looking robe with a high collar visible at the neck. His left hand is raised to his chest, grasping a scepter or staff. The background is intricately designed with an ornate frame enclosing the portrait, featuring floral motifs and a lined pattern. At the bottom of the image, there is a text panel containing Latin inscriptions, with the name "IACOBVS I. REX. SCOTORVM," identifying him as King James I of Scotland, and additional Latin text below the portrait. The entire composition is in black and white.
